landing.heroSub: Pick your MacBook, drop stickers onto a lid that's exactly the real size, and print a 1:1 guide that lines up on the real thing.
landing.heroNote: No account needed. Works on your phone.
landing.story1: Start with your exact lid: width, height, corner radius and logo, in millimetres.
landing.story2: Calibrate once with any bank or ID card so the screen shows true size.
landing.story3: Drop stickers in. Every one keeps its real size as you move, turn and layer it.
landing.story4: Print the 1:1 guide. Lay it on your MacBook and stick through the outlines.
landing.statAccuracyLabel: printed accuracy, checked with a ruler
landing.statScaleLabel: vector PDF with a 100 mm calibration line
landing.step1Body: Choose the model and lid colour. Dimensions come from the maker's published specs.
landing.step2Body: Upload photos of your stickers or use ours. Set their size in mm, or measure them against a card or coin.
landing.step3Body: Export a 1:1 PDF, tiled across A4 or Letter if needed, plus a coordinate sheet.
landing.shopsBody: Soon you'll try stickers from independent shops on your lid at real size, then buy the whole layout in one checkout.

faq.q: Will it really be actual size?
faq.a: Yes. Everything is stored in millimetres. After a one-time calibration with a bank or ID card, the editor draws your lid at real size, and the PDF prints at exact physical dimensions.

faq.q: How do I know my printout is right?
faq.a: Every page has a ruler that must measure exactly 100 mm. Print at 100% / Actual size, not "Fit to page", and check it with a real ruler.

faq.q: My MacBook lid is bigger than my paper.
faq.a: The PDF tiles the lid across several A4 or Letter sheets with overlap strips and crosshairs so you can tape them together precisely.
No. Your layouts save on this device and you can share a link. Sign in with Google to keep them together in your collection; cloud saves and buying come later.

faq.q: Can I use photos of my own stickers?
faq.a: Yes. Upload or take a photo, remove the background, then set the real size by typing it, picking a preset, or marking a card or coin in the photo.
